title: Taskbar/Start-menu MVVM redesign: background shell-model service + observable collections + off-thread cached icons (never block UI thread)
description: User-directed architecture fix. Root problem: shell does model work on the UI thread and mutates the view imperatively. Target: (1) background ShellModel service owning ObservableCollection<TaskButton> (windows) + ObservableCollection<Program> (apps) + async icon cache, all updated off the UI thread; (2) TaskbarViewModel/StartMenuViewModel thin projections; (3) view = virtualized ItemsControl + DataTemplate, no hand-rolled UpsertButton/Items.Add; (4) icons render off-thread (Task.Run) cached by (path,size), lazy per visible item; (5) enumerate apps warm at startup off-thread. Decisions: Full MVVM (not incremental); model lives in a dedicated background service (not the view-model). Also fix settings load to not block UI thread. See bd memory never-block-ui-thread.
notes:
Added requirement: taskbar button changes ANIMATED like Windows XP — buttons fade/grow in when a window opens, fade/shrink out when it closes, and width changes (as the strip fills) transition smoothly. Implement via Avalonia Transitions on the button DataTemplate (Opacity+Width) for add + resize; exit animation coordinated by ShellModel delaying the collection Remove (set IsClosing → animate → remove after ~150ms, via a non-blocking DispatcherTimer/Task.Delay+Post, never blocking the UI thread).
STATUS 2026-07-12 (uncommitted): TASKBAR portion DONE (background ShellModel + observable collections + off-thread cached icons + data-bound ItemsControl replacing imperative buttons + XP width/opacity animations 250ms + 2s reconcile prune). PENDING USER VERIFY: animations actually animate live; disappear works. NOT DONE: START MENU rewire — bind Programs to ShellModel.Programs as a virtualized ItemsControl, instant open, lazy icons (ProgramItemViewModel.EnsureIcon already written but unused; StartMenu.axaml.cs still on the old eager 284-icon path that froze ~2s). Next concrete step = rewrite StartMenu to bind + virtualize.

title: Startup deadlock: SettingsService.LoadAsync().GetResult() on UI thread hangs when settings.json exists
description: App.axaml.cs OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted blocks the Avalonia UI thread with settings.LoadAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(). LoadAsync awaits File.ReadAllTextAsync with default ConfigureAwait(true), so the continuation is posted back to the blocked UI SynchronizationContext -> deadlock. Only triggers when ~/.config/bevel/settings.json EXISTS (first run skips the await via File.Exists gate, so it went unnoticed in bevel-wym). Symptoms: process alive + foreground GUI app but zero windows on screen, and ignores SIGTERM (RequestExit posts Shutdown to the non-pumping dispatcher). Exposed by bevel-0ml taskbarRows persistence which guarantees the file exists. Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on the file I/O awaits in SettingsService so it is safe to block on from the UI thread. Diagnosed via macOS 'sample': main-thread parked in Monitor_Wait/SyncBlock::Wait.
notes: FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE (uncommitted). Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on SettingsService LoadAsync/SaveAsync/UpdateAsync file I/O + moved the startup LoadAsync().GetResult() from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted to Program.Main BEFORE StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime (loads before the thread becomes the UI thread). App now shows windows + honours SIGTERM even with settings.json present. Ready to commit.
close_reason: Verified fix present in working tree: SettingsService Load/Save/UpdateAsync all use ConfigureAwait(false) on file I/O (SettingsService.cs:61,105,112,119); startup load moved to Program.Main:48 before StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime; App.axaml.cs no longer blocks the UI thread on LoadAsync. Verified live per bead notes.

title: Shell chrome tooltips leak into taskbar window list (split mode)
description:
In split-process mode the taskbar/desktop role processes ran macOS .regular activation policy, so their own transient popups (tooltips, menus) passed the Swift helper's window filter, got registered as foreign taskbar entries, shifted the bar, and the layout/focus churn dismissed the tooltips. The helper's reserved-title exclusion ('Bevel Taskbar'/'Bevel Desktop') never matched — the CG window title is the generic 'Avalonia Application'.

Fix: mark the taskbar and desktop role processes .accessory (NSApplicationActivationPolicyAccessory) at startup via new Bevel.Pal.MacOS.ShellActivation.HideFromDock(), called from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted for ShellRole.Taskbar/Desktop. This is correct shell identity (no Dock tile, out of Cmd-Tab) AND makes the helper's existing activationPolicy==.regular filter drop ALL their windows (main + tooltips), title-independent. Not applied to All mode: that process also hosts the file-manager window, which should appear in the taskbar; activation policy can't distinguish it from a tooltip in the same process (needs window-level/subrole filtering instead).
notes: CORRECTION to earlier close: the .accessory change (ShellActivation.HideFromDock) did NOT fix the phantom-button/tooltip bug — it only affects the FILTERED snapshot path (describe) and shell Dock identity. Real root cause: the Swift helper's AX-observer event path (enqueueAXEvent -> buildTaskbarWindowFromAX -> broadcast) broadcast .opened for EVERY window an observed app created, bypassing describe()'s filters, so the shell's own .accessory tooltip/menu popups (a flood of empty-title 'Avalonia Application' windows) leaked as phantom taskbar buttons until the 2s snapshot reconcile pruned them. Fix: gate enqueueAXEvent on NSRunningApplication(pid).activationPolicy == .regular, mirroring describe(). Diagnosed via new BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR=1 taskbar logging (176 phantom ADDs in one hover session). Also fixed: clock tooltip flicker (PlacementMode.Top so it isn't under the cursor).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified. Taskbar/desktop role processes now set .accessory via ShellActivation.HideFromDock() in App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted. Verified on running split shell: lsappinfo reports both as type=UIElement; helper debug log shows 'drop ... Avalonia Application pid=<taskbar/desktop> reason=activationPolicy=1'; real foreign apps (Finder, Firefox, Chrome, Claude, ...) still kept; 0 errors.

title: Harden WindowServiceImpl.swift concurrency & observer lifecycle
description: Code review (swift-ios persona) flagged pre-existing thread-safety and lifecycle issues in native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/WindowServiceImpl.swift: (P1) unsynchronized mutation of lastForeignFrontmostPID; (P1) broadcast() does not actually serialize writer.write() despite the writeQueue/comment; (P1) AXObserver refcon passUnretained with no sync against in-flight callbacks during shutdown/deinit; (P2) Changes-stream subscribers never removed on client disconnect; (P2) per-instance NSWorkspace observer never removed; (P2) force-casts on CFTypeRef from third-party AX servers can crash the daemon; (P3) addObserver doesn't check isShutdown. Pre-existing (not this session), so out of the review's apply scope — filed for follow-up.
design: Serialize writer.write via the existing writeQueue (actual queue.sync/async, not just a comment); guard lastForeignFrontmostPID under stateLock; remove per-client subscribers on disconnect and the NSWorkspace observer on shutdown/deinit; replace force-casts (as!) on AX CFTypeRef with conditional casts + safe fallback; gate addObserver on isShutdown. Consider a TSan run in CI to catch the data races.
acceptance_criteria: No unsynchronized shared-state access (TSan clean on a representative session); writer.write serialized; observers/subscribers removed on disconnect/shutdown; AX value casts are non-crashing.
close_reason: All 7 findings fixed in WindowServiceImpl.swift (+339/-98); swift build clean + 33 tests 0 failures, independently re-verified. (1,P1) lastForeignFrontmostPID read-modify-write now inside a single stateLock.withLock block, lock released before any AX call. (2,P1) broadcast() serializes writer.write via writeQueue.async + DispatchSemaphore (ordered, one-at-a-time, no deadlock for on-queue callers). (3,P2) Changes subscribers removed on disconnect via defer+while(!Task.isCancelled). (4,P2) NSWorkspace didLaunch observer token captured + removed in shutdown/deinit. (5,P2) all five AX/CF force-casts replaced with CFGetTypeID guards + safe fallback so a hostile AX server can't crash the daemon. (6,P1) AXObserver refcon dangling-callback race closed: run-loop source removal marshalled onto the AX run-loop thread (performOnAXRunLoopSync) before CFRunLoopStop, teardown closure captures only locals. (7,P3) addObserver early-returns when isShutdown. Invariants preserved: describe() sole descriptor builder, isShellChrome layer-0 filter untouched.

title: Helper: new windows detected up to ~1s late (AX observers + launch hook were inert — no run loop)
description: ROOT CAUSE: AXObserver run-loop sources were added to CFRunLoopGetCurrent() inside the poll Task (cooperative-pool thread, never runs a CFRunLoop), so kAXWindowCreatedNotification never fired and the 1s reconcile poll was the ONLY detector. FIX (IMPLEMENTED + LIVE, awaiting user verification): WindowServiceImpl.startAXRunLoopThread() spins a dedicated Thread running CFRunLoopRun(); AX observer sources now added to that run loop (axRunLoop) via addObserver(for:); NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification hook registers a launching app's observer before its first window; reconcile poll 1s->500ms backstop. Files: native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/WindowServiceImpl.swift. Helper builds + runs; NOT yet confirmed faster by user.
notes: CODE-VERIFIED post-bevel-8l6 (2026-07-13). Confirmed present & coherent: init (line 132-137) calls startAXRunLoopThread() FIRST, blocking on axRunLoopReady.wait() until the dedicated 'bevel.ax.runloop' Thread publishes axRunLoop + arms the didLaunchApplication hook, THEN startReconciliationPoll(). AX observer sources now attach to that run loop (addObserver/ensureObservers, lines 1030-1065) which actually runs CFRunLoopRun() (1021), with a no-op NSMachPort (1020) keeping it parked when sourceless. Launch hook registers a launching app's observer pre-first-window (1007-1015). Poll backstop 500ms (1151). shutdown() removes launch hook + tears down observers before CFRunLoopStop. Fully integrated with 8l6 refcon-safety (performOnAXRunLoopSync teardown). swift build clean + 33 Swift tests 0 failures, independently re-run. title: Taskbar missing Finder folder windows entirely
description: Finder folder/browser windows never get a taskbar button. Helper debug showed 'drop cg=1618 Finder reason=no-title hasAX=false' — the describe()/filter path drops Finder windows (no AX title / hasAX=false). Fix the helper enumeration so Finder folder windows are captured with their folder-name title. Queued by user 2026-07-12 as next-batch.
notes: FIX IMPLEMENTED + code-verified (2026-07-13), live confirmation pending. ROOT CAUSE: correlateAXElements documented a frame-comparison fallback (class doc + method doc) that was never implemented — only the _AXUIElementGetWindow SPI path ran. Finder folder windows don't resolve via that SPI, so they never entered axMap → describe() sees hasAX=false → AX-title fallback skipped → empty kCGWindowName (no Screen Recording) → dropped at the no-title gate. FIX: implemented the documented fallback — correlateAXElements now takes the CG entries, groups by owner PID, and when the SPI fails matches the AX window to a same-PID CG window by frame (kAXPosition/kAXSize vs kCGWindowBounds, both top-left origin). Guardrails: zero-area AX frames never match (keeps title-less phantoms out of axMap), already-claimed CGIDs skipped (no two AX windows collapse onto one CG window), same-PID only (no cross-app frame collisions). New helpers axWindowFrame + frameMatchedCGID (testable). describe() remains sole descriptor builder (verified: 1 occurrence); isShellChrome/minimized-exempt/titleForStableDiff/zero-frame/activation-policy invariants unchanged. 5 new unit tests; swift build clean + 38 tests 0 failures, independently re-run. title: Cross-volume file op races on shared List (corruption/lost undo)
description: FileOperationService.ExecuteByVolumeAsync (:862) runs one Task.Run per volume concurrently via Task.WhenAll; the SemaphoreSlim(1,1) is per-volume so it does NOT serialize across volumes. Job callbacks mutate shared results/undoPairs/copiedPaths lists (ExecuteMoveAsync :218-247, ExecuteCopyAsync :371-394) with no lock. A single operation spanning two volumes (internal disk + USB) races on List<T>.Add -> corrupted backing array, lost/duplicated results, or IndexOutOfRangeException aborting the op and leaving an incomplete undo stack. Fix: guard the shared collections (lock or per-volume local lists merged after WhenAll).
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent multi-volume copy/move records every result and undo pair with no race.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. FileOperationService: locked shared result/undo collections (w15), safe _cts lifecycle with gate+clear-before-dispose and CTS passed down to avoid cross-cancel (tbo), read-only dest fails fast (c7l), single destination resolve via TryResolveAsync (5ty, plus LocalFsProvider type-desc dedup/dead-code/delete-branch collapse). New FileOperationServiceTests + FileOperationServiceProviderTests (11 tests). Core 57/57, FileManager 20/20.

title: App bootstrap bypasses DI: ComputerProvider/Settings/FileOps never wired

Because App never resolves these from App.Services: (1) 'My Computer' navigation hits GetProvider("computer") -> KeyNotFoundException (silently empty pane); (2) _settings stays null so Tools>Folder Options is a no-op (FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs:81); (3) _fileOps stays null so Undo/Ctrl+Z is a no-op (:87,:490). Fix: resolve VfsRoot, SettingsService, FileOperationService, and the window from App.Services and call the setters (or inject via ctor).

description: A supervisor (shell-core, or a thin launcher role) spawns + crash-restarts the role processes, extending the HelperLifecycle/HelperProcessHost monitor-loop pattern (already supports multiple children). title: M1: per-capability RPC auth scoping for helper services (ScriptingService/InputService)
description: M0's helper exposes only SupervisionService (Ping), gated by the per-session nonce — one token grants everything. M1 adds ScriptingService (Apple Events) and InputService (synthetic input), which are strictly more dangerous; a single all-or-nothing token means any code that can read the token (or any future in-proc plugin) gets input synthesis for free. Implement the capability-scoped design from bevel-vgg (see design field) before those services ship.
design:
Design (bevel-vgg item 3, 2026-07-10):
1. TOKEN FORMAT: keep one 16-byte session nonce as the MAC key, but per-RPC auth becomes 'x-bevel-token: <capability>:<HMAC-SHA256(nonce, capability)>' where capability ∈ {supervision, scripting, input}. The helper derives the expected MAC per capability at startup from --token; constant-time compare as today (SupervisionServiceImpl pattern).
2. SCOPING: HelperClient.Connect gains a capability set; Bevel.Ipc exposes typed sub-clients (SupervisionClient, ScriptingClient, InputClient) each attaching only its own capability header. App composition decides which sub-clients a component receives — e.g. the AE dispatcher gets scripting but never input.
3. HELPER SIDE: each Swift service impl validates ONLY its own capability's MAC, so a leaked scripting MAC cannot call InputService. Unknown/missing capability → RPCError(.unauthenticated), same as today.
4. NO NEW SECRETS: everything derives from the existing nonce; no extra key exchange, rotation still per-session via helper relaunch.
5. TESTS: contract tests assert cross-capability rejection (scripting MAC on input RPC fails), and Bevel.Ipc unit tests assert each sub-client sends exactly its own header. Extend Bevel.Pal.ContractTests.
Deliberately NOT chosen: separate nonces per capability via env (env size/leak surface grows), and TLS/mTLS on the UDS (overkill under 0700 dir + same-user threat model).

title: ComputerProvider: volume names with '/' break VfsPath round-trip on macOS (resolve/navigate fails)
description: GetVolumeDisplayName embeds the native mount path in parentheses, Windows-style ('Local Disk (C:)'). On macOS mount paths contain '/' — e.g. 'Macintosh HD (/)' or '/System/Volumes/Data/home (/System/Volumes/Data/home)' — and for the root drive Name.TrimEnd('/') even yields an empty string. Since VfsPath segments split on '/', node.Path.FileName is mangled, so ResolveAsync(node.Path) throws DirectoryNotFoundException ('Volume not found: ()') and ResolveEffectivePath never matches — clicking a volume under My Computer cannot resolve it by path. Repro: enumerate computer:// root, then ResolveAsync(first.Path). The UDS lives in a world-accessible temp dir (Path.GetTempPath()/bevel-helper, HelperLifecycle.cs:44), so any local process can call the helper. title: FileOperationService._cts shared field: dispose/cross-cancel race
description: FileOperationService.cs:63-64 assigns the per-call 'using' linked CTS to the shared field _cts; Cancel() (:81) and in-job _cts?.Cancel() (:223,:376) read it with no synchronization. After ExecuteAsync returns the linked CTS is disposed but _cts still points to it -> a later UI Cancel() throws ObjectDisposedException. Two overlapping ExecuteAsync calls clobber _cts so operation A's internal cancel actually cancels operation B. Fix: pass the CTS through the call graph instead of a shared field, or track per-operation state and null/guard _cts on completion.

Fix: guard OnNext against disposal (dispose flag + lock, or check _subject.IsDisposed) and swallow post-dispose notifications.

title: HelperClient gRPC 'unix://' channel has no ConnectCallback -> never connects
description: src/Bevel.Ipc/HelperClient.cs:25-31 builds GrpcChannel.ForAddress('unix://<path>') with only Insecure credentials and no SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback opening a UnixDomainSocketEndPoint. Grpc.Net.Client cannot dial a UDS without that callback, so PingAsync never connects and HelperLifecycle.WaitForReadyAsync (:109) times out after 5s. Currently masked because the host is never started (see bevel-c0y), but this blocks the helper the moment that is fixed. Fix: set GrpcChannelOptions.HttpHandler = new SocketsHttpHandler { ConnectCallback = ... UnixDomainSocketEndPoint(socketPath) } and use http://localhost as the address.
acceptance_criteria: HelperClient.PingAsync connects to the helper over the Unix domain socket.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. title: SearchPaneViewModel.StopSearch disposes CTS still in use by the walk
description: SearchPaneViewModel.cs:104-110: WalkAsync is fire-and-forget (:100) and keeps enumerating with _searchCts.Token, but StopSearch calls Cancel() then Dispose() then null. Disposing a CTS whose token is still registered inside 'await foreach' throws ObjectDisposedException (not OperationCanceledException), escaping the catch(OperationCanceledException) filters and becoming an unobserved task exception. Triggered on every Stop / new-search-while-running. Fix: don't Dispose the CTS until the walk task has completed (await it, or dispose in a continuation), or swap-then-dispose the old CTS after the task ends.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling or restarting a search never throws ObjectDisposedException.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). title: LocalFsProvider enumerate: uncaught GetAttributes TOCTOU aborts whole listing
description: LocalFsProvider.cs:45 calls File.GetAttributes(entry) inside the EnumerateFileSystemEntries loop with no try/catch. If another process deletes/moves the entry between enumeration and GetAttributes, it throws FileNotFoundException/IOException and the whole IAsyncEnumerable terminates -> pane shows partial/zero items instead of skipping the vanished entry. Reproducible in busy folders (Downloads, build/temp). Fix: wrap the per-entry stat in try/catch and 'continue' on transient IO/not-found.
acceptance_criteria: Enumerating a folder while entries vanish yields the surviving entries without aborting.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: HelperLifecycle restart spawns duplicate monitor loops
description: HelperLifecycle.cs: on exit detection MonitorLoopAsync (:167) calls LaunchAndConnectAsync, which unconditionally assigns a NEW _monitorCts and a NEW _monitorTask=MonitorLoopAsync(...) (:101-102). The current loop keeps running under its old, now-unreferenced token (never cancelled). After N crashes there are N+1 concurrent monitor loops; the next crash makes all of them KillHelper()+relaunch simultaneously -> duplicate helper processes, orphaned CTSs, NRE races on _helperProcess. StopAsync only cancels the latest CTS. Fix: restart in-place within the existing loop (don't recurse into LaunchAndConnectAsync's monitor-spawn), or cancel/await the prior loop before starting a new one.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated helper crashes leave exactly one monitor loop and one helper process.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. HelperLifecycle: single self-healing monitor loop started once in StartAsync (never spawns duplicates on restart), non-blocking graceful start (missing/broken helper no longer aborts boot — enables host start), backoff on repeated failures (mox). New Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests: HelperLifecycleTests (3) + HelperClientTests (4), 7/7 green.

title: ItemView.SortAsync drops items streamed during sort + virtualization crash

Also, unlike SortItems (:280 nulls ItemsPresenter.ItemsSource first 'to avoid virtualization teardown crash'), SortAsync mutates the still-bound collection, risking that crash. Fix: detach ItemsSource before mutating; re-apply the sort to the live collection (or merge post-sort additions) instead of replacing with a stale snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Sorting a large directory mid-stream keeps all items and does not crash.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. title: Route taskbar window-icon PNG path (ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon) through the shared BGRA pool
description: gww.6 landed the pool behind IIconProvider (installed-app/Start-menu icons). ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon still decodes each ForeignWindow.IconPng (raw PNG over the wire) into an Avalonia Bitmap per-window, uncached — so N windows of the same app re-decode the same PNG. To route it through MmfBgraPool: derive a stable key (content hash of the PNG, since window icons have no path key), decode PNG->BGRA once, TryGet/TryAdd against the pool, and wrap the PalImage via PalImageBitmap.ToBitmap for the VM. Lower value than the IIconProvider path (window icons are per-window + transient) and touches the hot taskbar path, so split out of gww.6.

Deliberately an in-process cache, NOT the shared MMF pool — window icons are process-local + transient and the pool is single-writer (the split taskbar is a reader; writing there would be a second writer). Full MMF sharing would need the core to decode ForeignWindow.IconPng into the pool (split-mode-only benefit); deferred. Build green; 74 taskbar tests pass.

title: P6: MMF-backed shared BGRA icon pool behind IIconProvider
description: Replace MacOSIconProvider._cache with a memory-mapped (CreateFromFile, macOS has no /dev/shm -> runtime dir) store of (w,h,BGRA) slots keyed path|size; each process's PalImageBitmap.ToBitmap wraps a view into the MMF instead of a private byte[]. Route the currently-uncached taskbar PNG path (ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon) through the same pool. Note: ~0.5MB/proc at 16px today (memory win is small); real payoff is decode-cost/consistency now + readiness for large/Retina icons. Named MMF is Windows-only; cross-process notify via shell-core, not named sync primitives (process-local on Unix).

Per-process writes serialized (pool is single-writer). Wired in CompositionRoot with 512-slot × 96×96 geometry co-located with the shell-core runtime dir. 3 PooledIconProviderTests (render-once, cross-instance reader-serve, reader-miss-fallback) + the pre-existing 9 MmfBgraPool tests green; full solution builds; 68 taskbar + 23 UI tests pass. title: Backstop-caught window close reorders the exiting button to the strip end
description: Cosmetic edge from the bevel-wak reconciler fold. The COMMON close path (OnWindowClosed event -> Remove -> BeginExit on the single VM) animates the button out IN PLACE, unchanged. But when a Close event is MISSED and the 2s backstop Reconcile() catches it, the shared ObservableReconciler's onRemove defers the leaving item while phase-2 compaction moves survivors to slots 0..n-1, pushing the closing button to the end of the strip — so it shrinks at the end instead of in place, ~2s after the window is already gone. Rare (only on dropped Close events) and low-impact. Proper fix would need the reconciler to PIN deferred-leaving items at their slot so survivors flow around them; deferred as not worth the complexity/live-tuning now. Verify/adjust live.
close_reason: Fixed in ObservableReconciler. Rewrote Reconcile to build an explicit finalOrder list and diff the collection to it, instead of pruning then compacting survivors to slots 0..n-1. title: App ignores SIGTERM: graceful-shutdown handler registered but process doesn't exit
description: Program.cs registers PosixSignalRegistration for SIGTERM/SIGINT -> App.RequestExit() -> Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(lifetime.Shutdown()). Observed during bevel-m2.13 work: kill (SIGTERM) leaves the app running; only kill -9 stops it. Pre-existing (not caused by the mitigator's Exit handler, which only cancels a CTS). Likely the classic desktop lifetime Shutdown() doesn't terminate the process while background loop tasks (window poll, mitigator) are alive, or RequestExit isn't reaching Shutdown. Repro: pgrep the app, kill <pid>, observe it survives. Fix: ensure Shutdown fully exits (or Environment.Exit fallback) so 'launchctl'/system logout can stop Bevel cleanly.
close_reason: Root cause: sync-over-async deadlock. After StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime returns, Avalonia's SynchronizationContext is still installed on the main thread; host.StopAsync().GetResult() blocked it, and StopAsync's await-continuation was posted back to that blocked thread -> hang (only kill -9 worked). Fix: run host.StopAsync via Task.Run (detached from the UI context) in Program.cs; root PosixSignalRegistrations with 'using'; ConfigureAwait(false) in HelperLifecycle.StopAsync. Verified: SIGTERM exits in ~1s with graceful cleanup (helper killed, no orphan).

title: AppKitInterop.NSStringCreate returns an autoreleased string but doc says 'caller must release' — callers over-free it

Found while implementing MacOSIconProvider (bevel-m2.15), which hit an intermittent segfault from exactly this until it stopped releasing the string. Fix: either make NSStringCreate retain (so the contract holds) or drop the release in callers and rely on an autorelease pool. Audit all NSStringCreate callers.

title: SearchPane content-search bypasses provider OpenReadAsync (file-scheme only)
description: Altitude finding. SearchPaneViewModel.cs:246 ContentMatchesAsync early-returns unless node.Path.Scheme=='file' and reads bytes via raw File.Exists/FileStream on node.Path.Value, bypassing the provider's OpenReadAsync that already abstracts reading any node's bytes. Content search is permanently blind to non-file providers (zip/net/trash) and assumes Path.Value is an OS path. Fix: read via the provider's OpenReadAsync so content search works for every scheme.
acceptance_criteria: Content search works for any provider implementing OpenReadAsync, not just file.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). ItemView.SortAsync: shared ApplyOrder detaches ItemsSource and never drops streamed late arrivals (rn9). New SearchPaneViewModelTests (4) + ItemViewSortTests (4). FileManager 28/28.

title: FileManagerWindow reimplements the tree + VfsRootLocator static global
description: Altitude finding. FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs:176 hand-rolls a second tree directly on TreeViewItem (placeholder sentinels, inline VFS enumeration, kind filtering) that duplicates TreePaneViewModel — but with no cancellation/off-thread handling, so slow-volume expansion blocks the UI thread. It relies on a process-global mutable static VfsRootLocator.Current (VfsRootLocator.cs) because the static expand handler can't capture instance state, which breaks with a second window/test. Fix: drive the tree through TreePaneViewModel (route VfsRoot via instance state) and delete VfsRootLocator.
acceptance_criteria: Tree uses TreePaneViewModel with cancellation/off-thread; no static VfsRoot global.
close_reason: Fixed core defect + tested. Tree expand/create handlers are now INSTANCE methods binding to the window's own _vfsRoot with a per-window _treeCts (cancellable); deleted the global mutable VfsRootLocator (broke with >1 window). Added OnClosed disposing _treeCts/_enumerateCts/watcher (also fixes the on-close CTS/watcher leak). Test: FileManagerWindowTreeTests proves two windows expand against their own roots. Full solution builds; FileManager 29/29.

title: VfsPath hardcodes '/' separator; duplicated vfs:// parsers
description: Altitude finding. VfsPath.Combine/ParentValue/FileName hardcode '/' while LocalFsProvider stores native OS paths in Value (breaks on Windows: Combine('C:\foo','bar')='C:\foo/bar'). There is no VfsPath.Parse, so call sites hand-roll vfs:// parsing two different ways (FileManagerWindow NavigateTo ~:244 via new Uri, SearchPaneViewModel.ParseLookInPath ~:274 via manual slicing) and will diverge. Fix: make VfsPath own canonical parsing/combination and normalize separators; route all vfs:// parsing through it.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical VfsPath parse/combine used everywhere; correct on mixed separators.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: Copy read-only-dest fallback writes to a read stream (NotSupportedException)
description: FileOperationService.cs:491-493 (CopyFileContentsAsync else branch): when GetMutatorAsync returns null (read-only destination) it opens destProvider.OpenReadAsync(destination) as the write target and calls readStream.CopyToAsync(writeStream) -> writing to a read-only stream throws NotSupportedException instead of a clean 'destination is read-only' error. Currently unreachable (only LocalFsProvider exists and always returns a mutator) but latent once a read-only provider lands. Fix: fail fast with a clear 'destination is read-only' error when the mutator is null.
acceptance_criteria: Copy to a read-only destination fails with a clear, correct error.
close_reason: Fixed + tested.
